fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Entry Area; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Landscaped Area
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the street in both directions.
• Identify and mark all secondary access points so responders can locate them quickly without walking the full perimeter.
• Keep at least one access point wide enough and unobstructed for a stretcher or equipment cart to pass through.
• Move parked vehicles out of the primary arrival area when possible to give responding units room to position.
• Keep the walkway from the parking area to the front entry clear of planters, decorations, or landscaping that narrows the path.
• Trim any landscaping along the walkway that reduces visibility of the front entry from the street or driveway.
• Designate and mark a flat, open staging area on the lawn where responding units can set down equipment clear of vehicle traffic.
• Post the property address at the front entry in addition to the street-facing location so responders can confirm they are at the correct door.
• Because turnaround space is limited, discuss with your local fire department whether a specific pull-forward or pull-aside parking position should be marked for arriving units.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Multiple Access Routes; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees in the cluster visible near the property to reduce the amount of connected vegetation that could carry fire toward the structure.
• Trim or remove shrubs and plants growing directly against or immediately next to the structure.
• Keep low branches on scattered trees trimmed up from the ground to reduce the chance of fire climbing into the canopy.
• Maintain open ground between the tree cluster and the structure by removing any shrubs or small plants filling the gap between them.
• Keep scattered shrubs trimmed low and separated from one another to avoid a continuous path of plants leading toward the structure.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
